item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Abiy Ahmed was **modestly closer by end-2024** to the regime’s economic-reform and regional-influence program than at the start, but the gain was uneven and fragile. The macro program moved from announcement to implementation, and the Somalia dispute ended the year in a diplomatic off-ramp. Against that, domestic coercion, civic-space repression, and low living standards remained severe, so the trajectory is positive only in a narrow, state-capacity sense.

**Accepted Claims**
- Title: `IMF Executive Board Approves Four-Year US$3.4 billion Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for Ethiopia` | Publisher: IMF | Date: 2024-07-29 | URL: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24291-ethiopia-imf-exec-board-approves-4yr-us3b-ecf-arr | Claim: The IMF framed Ethiopia’s package as a comprehensive reform program to stabilize macroeconomic imbalances, move to a market-determined exchange rate, cut inflation, restore debt sustainability, and expand social safety nets. This is strong evidence that Abiy’s program had a clear, executable direction by mid-2024. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.8, 8B.9
- Title: `IMF Executive Board Completes the First Review under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for Ethiopia` | Publisher: IMF | Date: 2024-10-18 | URL: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/10/18/pr-24383-ethiopia-imf-completes-the-1st-review-under-the-ecf-arrangement | Claim: The IMF said all quantitative performance criteria and four of five structural benchmarks were met, the FX transition had proceeded with little disruption, and the program was advancing well. That is the clearest evidence that the reform agenda had moved materially closer to delivery by year-end. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.8, 8B.9
- Title: `World Bank Backs Ethiopia's Reforms to Promote Sustainable and Inclusive Growth, Enhance Resilience, and Take Climate Action` | Publisher: World Bank | Date: 2024-07-30 | URL: https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/30/world-bank-backs-ethiopia-s-reforms-to-promote-sustainable-and-inclusive-afe-growth | Claim: The World Bank said the reform package would expand private-sector orientation, improve fiscal transparency, strengthen SOE performance, and expand social safety nets. This supports a reading that the government was moving further into its chosen economic model rather than stalling. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.8
- Title: `Ethiopia passes law to open banking to foreign competition` | Publisher: Reuters via Indian Express | Date: 2024-12-17 | URL: https://indianexpress.com/article/news-today/ethiopia-parliament-law-banking-foreign-competition-9730148/ | Claim: Parliament opened banking to foreign competition, part of a broader opening of a tightly controlled sector. This is a concrete late-year sign that the policy program had advanced beyond rhetoric into structural liberalization. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.8
- Title: `Ethiopia-Somalia Ankara Declaration under facilitation of Republic of Türkiye` | Publisher: Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications | Date: 2024-12-12 | URL: https://www.iletisim.gov.tr/English/haberler/detay/ethiopia-somalia-ankara-declaration-under-facilitation-of-republic-of-turkiye | Claim: Ethiopia and Somalia reaffirmed sovereignty, set aside disputes, and committed to cooperation toward shared prosperity. This is the clearest evidence that Abiy ended the year in a better position on the Horn dispute than at the start. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.9
- Title: `Abiy publicly denied war intent with Somalia` | Publisher: Associated Press via CityNews | Date: 2024-02-06 | URL: https://kitchener.citynews.ca/2024/02/06/ethiopias-leader-plays-down-fears-of-conflict-with-somalia-over-a-planned-naval-port/ | Claim: Abiy said he had no intention of going to war with Somalia and framed peace as mutually beneficial. This is weak-to-moderate early-year evidence of a diplomatic off-ramp that later became real by December. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.9
- Title: `Ethiopia signs pact to use Somaliland's Red Sea port` | Publisher: Reuters, republished by MarketScreener | Date: 2024-01-01 | URL: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Landlocked-Ethiopia-signs-pact-to-use-Somaliland-s-Red-Sea-port-45654814/ | Claim: The Berbera MOU tied port access to possible naval use and political concessions, and was widely treated as destabilizing. This is strong evidence that Abiy began the year with a risky move that moved him away from a stable end-state before he partially corrected course. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.9
- Title: `Ethiopia authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent` | Publisher: Amnesty International | Date: 2024-02-19 | URL: https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/ | Claim: Amnesty said the state of emergency was used for warrantless arrests, curbs on movement, and bans on assemblies and associations. This is strong evidence that domestic consolidation was being pursued through coercion, not durable institutional broadening. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.9
- Title: `Ethiopia: Authorities Suspend Three Rights Groups` | Publisher: Human Rights Watch | Date: 2024-12-02 | URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups | Claim: The government suspended three rights organizations while Abiy publicly praised reforms such as media freedom and NGO registration. This is the clearest late-year sign that civic-space repression remained central, limiting how far the regime had actually advanced in durable legitimacy. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.9
- Title: `Ethiopia Poverty and Equity Brief: October 2024` | Publisher: World Bank | Date: 2024-10-01 | URL: https://documents.worldbank.org/pt/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099729001032529868 | Claim: The World Bank said living standards deteriorated across the country because of multiple shocks and that poverty was expected to have increased significantly since 2016. This is the strongest counterweight to any simple “the country is clearly better off” reading by year-end. | QIDs: 8B.10
- Title: `Ethiopia: Military Executes Dozens in Amhara Region` | Publisher: Human Rights Watch | Date: 2024-04-04 | URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region | Claim: HRW reported federal forces summarily killed dozens of civilians in Merawi. This is strong evidence that domestic coercion remained a severe liability for durable regime success and undercut broad progress claims. | QIDs: 8B.10, 8B.9

**Search Gap**
- There is no single source that directly scores “closer to the program than at the start,” so this conclusion is inferential.
- The best evidence is strongest on the economic file and the Somalia de-escalation, weaker on whether coercive domestic control was durable or politically sustainable.
- I found no reliable public evidence that the government had solved the domestic-security problem by year-end; the reform progress is real, but so are the countervailing shocks and repression.
